---
title: "Homework 4: Flood and Cold-Weather Risk"
---

## Overview

For this assignment you will create a well-designed knitted .html report intended for emergency management decision-makers to support natural hazard decision making.

You are an employee at North Carolina Emergency Management (NCEM). You have been asked to use recent and historical environmental data to support preparedness decisions for two hazard scenarios.

## Scenario 1: Flood Risk at Bolin Creek

After Hurricane Chantal caused severe flooding along Bolin Creek in July 2025, local officials are reconsidering whether they need a more proactive monitoring plan for periods when repeated high-water days are possible. NCEM wants to know how often unusually high-water conditions occur and whether the likelihood of several flood-risk days within a short period is large enough to justify enhanced monitoring or preparedness measures. (The gauge data end on January 1, 2025, so Chantal itself is not in the record.)

## Scenario 2: Low-Temperature Risk

NCEM has funding to open one additional warming shelter in North Carolina. The western part of the state is already relatively well-prepared for cold weather, so the new shelter should be located elsewhere. NCEM needs a recommendation for a county that faces meaningful cold-weather risk and has at least one additional vulnerability, exposure, or hazard concern that would make a warming shelter especially useful.

## Task

Create a well-organized knitted .html report for emergency management decision-makers. The report should contain separate sections for the Bolin Creek flood-risk analysis and the statewide cold-temperature analysis. Within each section, integrate analysis, visualization, and interpretation throughout rather than presenting them as separate components. At a minimum, your report should:

- Calculate the empirical probability of a "flood-risk day" at Bolin Creek. A flood-risk day is a day when the water height is more than 1.5 ft higher than the median daily height for the period of record (2015–2025).
- Use this empirical probability to determine the most likely number of flood-risk days over a 25-day period, and calculate the probability of having more than 3 flood-risk days over a 25-day period.
- NCEM is considering whether to activate an enhanced flood monitoring protocol during 25-day periods when repeated flood-risk days are possible. Using your probability calculations, evaluate whether the likelihood of more than 3 flood-risk days is high enough to justify additional preparedness measures, and explain how your statistical results support your recommendation.
- Use the normal distribution to calculate, for each ASOS station, the probability of a January day with a maximum temperature below 32°F, and create a statewide probability map of cold-temperature risk.
- Recommend one county for a new warming shelter. Your recommendation should combine estimated cold-weather risk, geographic context, and at least one additional vulnerability, exposure, or hazard factor of your choosing. Do not choose a county in the west.

## Data

In your .Rmd, add a chunk for loading libraries and reading in data, and paste in this code:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

#Bolin Creek gauge readings, 2015-2025
bolin_creek_data <- read_csv("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1eEzriJ5XzR-aS74nJmyiQFVrmV4T3cel")

#January highs at NC ASOS stations, 2000-2019
asos_jan_data <- read_csv("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1_zE1kcC7YY083R6rv20sqeN1l2dCdmhi")

#daily maximum water height at Bolin Creek
max_bolin_creek <- bolin_creek_data |> group_by(time) |> summarise(max_water = max(value))
```

When you map the ASOS stations, longitude goes first: `st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)`.

Submit your polished knitted .html to the Homework 4 assignment on Canvas.

## Rubric (10 Points)

| Part | Points | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Analysis and visualizations | 4 | Correctly calculates flood-risk and cold-temperature probabilities (2); appropriate visualizations for the Bolin Creek analysis (0.5); complete, well-designed statewide probability map with clear legend, appropriate classification and readable layout (1); correctly applies probability concepts to the 25-day flood-risk scenario (0.5) |
| Discussion | 6 | Interprets flood-risk patterns and evaluates whether enhanced monitoring is justified (1.5); describes statewide cold-temperature risk patterns (1); clear, evidence-based warming shelter recommendation that includes additional vulnerability or hazard considerations (1.5); integrates statistics, visualizations and maps into a cohesive discussion (1); polished, well-organized report appropriate for emergency management decision-makers (1) |
